tasks.short: Prepare campaign budgets, test cost assumptions and submit estimates for approval.

steps.what: Retrieve previous campaign costs, current commitments and budget limits.
Request supplier quotes and clarify scope, rates and commercial assumptions.
Enter quoted rates, quantities and exclusions into the budget workbook.

loop.input: Supplier quote documents and scope clarifications.
loop.output: Draft cost lines with units, currency, tax treatment, exclusions and source references.
loop.check: Validate required fields and arithmetic; the manager confirms material rates, exclusions and ambiguous terms.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per quote; ambiguous lines return for manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier quotes use varied layouts and prose qualifications. Structured supplier forms would remove this loop.

steps.what: Calculate campaign costs, contingencies and alternative spend scenarios.
Choose scope, contingency and trade-offs against campaign objectives.
Prepare the budget submission with assumptions and supporting quotes.
Review affordability, challenge assumptions and approve the campaign budget.
Record the approved estimate against the campaign and cost centre.

tasks.design: Read commitments and actuals from the {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT}, then calculate scenarios with a versioned cost model on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded quote-extraction loop supplies reviewed cost lines, deterministic templates produce the submission in the {DOCS}, and an approved budget updates the {ERP} and {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier quotes differed in format, cost models were copied between workbooks, and finance records needed manual reconciliation.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic calculation and document generation were already feasible. Cheaper integration work and bounded extraction make the remaining document handling practical.
tasks.still_hard: Quotes may exclude production changes, usage rights or cancellation costs. Forecast response and the right contingency remain judgement calls.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate comparable scope, challenge optimistic assumptions and choose which campaign risks deserve contingency.

ambition.what: Refresh campaign cost-to-complete decisions whenever a material supplier quote changes.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time entering rates, repairing formulas and formatting submissions, and more time negotiating scope and evaluating alternatives. Spending and budget approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Compare campaign investment options against commercial objectives.
reach.learn: Contribution margin, incremental returns and sensitivity analysis.

reach.task: Build an event cost estimate with cancellation and attendance scenarios.
reach.learn: Fixed versus variable costs, contractual deadlines and contingency planning.

evidence.claim: Versioned rules can calculate quantities, rates, tax assumptions, contingencies and scenario totals without a model.
Variable supplier documents can use bounded extraction with source references and human confirmation.

assumptions: The budget workbook is a typical bridge between supplier documents and finance records.
Finance supplies approved currency, tax, contingency and cost-centre rules.
The extraction loop is needed only for quotes without reliable structured fields.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act requirements are assessed for the actual data and use.
Build estimates cover a limited campaign-cost model, access review and applicable national consultation.
The automation prior fits calculation and submission preparation; commercial negotiation and approval remain human.
unknowns: Which finance exports or interfaces are available?
How many suppliers provide structured quotes?
Which tax, currency and contingency rules apply?
Who approves budgets, and what are the approval thresholds?
Do access changes trigger employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Can existing finance configuration provide scenario calculation and submission templates?
How reliably can quote exclusions and usage-rights terms be extracted from representative documents?
Can approved estimates be written back with version history and duplicate prevention?
new_work: Review extracted rates, exclusions and ambiguous quote terms.
Maintain calculation rules, templates and approved rate tables.
Reconcile failed or duplicate finance updates.
Review scenarios when campaign scope or supplier terms change.
tasks.statement: Prepare budgets and submit estimates for program costs as part of campaign plan development.

tasks.short: Plan campaigns and prepare promotional concepts with commercial teams and agencies.

steps.what: Discuss audience needs, commercial goals, constraints, and agency expectations.
Collect product facts, previous results, and brand guidance from the {DOCS} and {BI}.
Agree the audience, proposition, channel mix, and proposed budget with commercial stakeholders.
Write the campaign brief and initial promotional concepts in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Campaign direction, approved product facts, brand guidelines, and brief template.
loop.output: Draft campaign brief and three promotional concepts with fact references.
loop.check: Validate required fields and fact references; the advertising manager checks originality, audience fit, and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per brief; missing facts or unresolved contradictions return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates fill factual sections, but propositions and creative concepts require writing from varied requirements.

steps.what: Resolve agency questions and reconcile sales, creative, and delivery expectations.
Assess revised concepts and select the proposal for production.
Approve the production scope and send the final brief to the agency.

tasks.design: A structured brief in the {WORKFLOW} links approved facts in the {DOCS}, results in the {BI}, and production tasks in the {PROJECT}. A bounded drafting loop proposes briefs and concepts; people settle the direction and agency disagreements. The {WORKFLOW} releases the production brief only after scope and budget approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Campaign requirements arrive through conversations, while facts, creative choices, and approvals sit in separate files and mail threads.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and approval flows handle routing. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and templates; bounded drafting helps with the free-text sections.
tasks.still_hard: A persuasive proposition, customer trust, agency negotiation, and agreement on commercial trade-offs remain difficult. Faster drafting does not prove sales impact.
tasks.human_edge: The manager recognises weak positioning, understands stakeholder motives, and takes responsibility for the creative bet.

ambition.what: A campaign brief service for small regional sales teams without dedicated creative support.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less fact gathering and brief assembly, with more customer discovery and concept testing. With delegated authority, the manager can authorise small concept tests within a fixed budget; larger commitments retain existing approval.

reach.task: Design a short audience concept test.
reach.learn: Sampling limits, neutral questions, and how to distinguish preference from likely purchase.

reach.task: Compare campaign options against commercial objectives.
reach.learn: Contribution margin, channel economics, and explicit trade-off decisions.

evidence.claim: HubSpot offers campaign planning and branded content drafting capabilities; this supports drafting feasibility, not autonomous creative approval.
Structured briefs, template assembly, and approval routing can use deterministic software; the proposed time shares and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: The planning cycle ends with production authorisation; asset production is covered separately.
The company has reusable product facts, brand guidance, and a budget approval process.
Build ranges cover one campaign workflow and a limited set of source connections.
Access work includes GDPR review of customer feedback and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which product facts are approved and who maintains them?
Can the relevant {DOCS}, {BI}, and {PROJECT} expose stable records or exports?
Which role can approve agency scope and budget?
Does customer feedback contain identifiable or confidential information?
Which employee consultation obligations apply?
research_questions: Which brief fields recur across recent campaigns?
Where do agency revisions arise: missing facts, unclear direction, or creative disagreement?
Does faster brief preparation create capacity for meaningful concept testing?
new_work: Review generated propositions and factual references.
Resolve missing or conflicting source facts.
Maintain brief templates, access permissions, and source connections.
Track whether brief quality reduces production revisions.
tasks.statement: Plan and prepare advertising and promotional material to increase sales of products or services, working with customers, company officials, sales departments, and advertising agencies.

tasks.short: Review and edit promotional materials against specifications, brand standards, and substantiated claims.

steps.what: Find the latest proof, approved brief, and specifications in the {DOCS}.
Check dimensions, duration, links, and required labels using an {OTHER} media editor.
Assess meaning, claims, tone, and visual context against the approved brief.

loop.input: Versioned proof, transcript where available, approved brief, brand guidance, and claim substantiation.
loop.output: Flagged passages or frames with rule references, evidence links, and uncertainty labels.
loop.check: Each flag identifies an exact passage or frame; the manager reviews the full proof and resolves contextual or legal questions.
loop.stop: One review pass per proof version; unreadable media, missing evidence, and uncertain claims go to a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Dimensions and required text are rule checks; implied claims and contextual meaning require interpretation.

steps.what: Edit copy and scripts in the {DOCS}, preserving approved facts and offer terms.

loop.input: Flagged copy or script, requested changes, approved facts, and protected offer terms.
loop.output: Tracked copy revisions and a change log.
loop.check: Compare protected facts, prices, dates, and terms; the manager checks meaning and tone before accepting revisions.
loop.stop: One revision and one correction pass per section; changes requiring new claims return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed replacements cover some edits, but preserving meaning while changing tone requires language generation.

steps.what: Apply layout and audiovisual revisions using an {OTHER} media editor.
Review the revised proof and approve or return the exact version.
Record approval and place the approved version in the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} assembles a versioned review pack from the {DOCS} and runs deterministic specification checks. Bounded loops flag contextual issues and propose tracked copy edits, while people assess the full asset and make visual revisions. Approval binds to the exact asset version before the {DOCS} makes it available for release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Review combines file inspection, contextual judgement, and approval across changing versions. Simple checklists cannot reliably assess implied claims or narrative meaning.
tasks.enabler_now: File metadata and specification checks are straightforward to automate. Bounded text and media interpretation can prepare evidence-linked review notes, with human judgement retained.
tasks.still_hard: Visual implication, humour, accessibility, rights clearance, and regulated claims need context. Extracted text or sampled frames can miss important content.
tasks.human_edge: The reviewer sees what an audience may infer and decides when an otherwise compliant asset would still damage trust.

ambition.what: A preflight review service for regional campaign teams before agency production.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from locating versions and checking specifications toward editorial judgement and coaching creators. Existing release accountability remains; any authority over regional assets requires explicit delegation.

reach.task: Create an evidence-based editorial standard for promotional claims.
reach.learn: Source hierarchy, implied claims, and clear reasons for accepting or rejecting wording.

reach.task: Review how layout changes alter meaning and accessibility.
reach.learn: Reading order, contrast, caption placement, and the limits of automated visual checks.

evidence.claim: Version-bound approvals, metadata checks, and evidence-linked review preparation are feasible patterns; reliable coverage requires testing on representative assets.
HubSpot offers branded content drafting; this supports copy assistance but does not establish reliable multimedia compliance review.
EU AI Act Article 50 contains transparency obligations relevant to certain synthetic content and deepfakes; applicability needs review.

assumptions: The initial scope covers common static assets and short scripts, with audiovisual coverage added only after validation.
The advertising manager can route specialist legal or rights questions to an authorised reviewer.
The workflow supports GDPR requirements and applicable EU AI Act transparency duties.
Access estimates include agency asset permissions and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which media formats and languages dominate the review queue?
Are specifications and claim substantiation current and machine-readable?
Which assets require specialist legal approval?
Can approval records be bound to immutable asset versions?
Which national advertising and employee consultation rules apply?
research_questions: Which recent defects were mechanical, contextual, or introduced after approval?
How often do extraction failures hide material information?
What false-positive rate would make review assistance slower than current practice?
new_work: Review flags and inspect content outside extracted text or sampled frames.
Maintain specification rules and approved claim references.
Test missed issues and false positives against real proofs.
Revoke approval when an asset changes.
Maintain escalation routes for rights, legal, and disclosure questions.
tasks.statement: Inspect layouts and advertising copy, and edit scripts, audio, video, and other promotional material for adherence to specifications.

tasks.short: Coordinate sales, creative, media, finance, and research work to deliver campaigns.

steps.what: Ask departmental leads for progress, dependencies, and blockers through the {EMAIL} and {CHAT}.
Reconcile departmental updates with dates and dependencies in the {PROJECT}.
Copy campaign status into a separate meeting pack in the {DOCS}.
Resolve conflicting priorities, resource constraints, and cross-department dependencies.
Confirm owners, revised dates, and resource commitments with departmental leads.
Record commitments in the {PROJECT} and circulate the action list through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure the {PROJECT} with shared milestones, dependency fields, owner updates, and deadline reminders through the {CHAT} or {EMAIL}. A live status view replaces the copied meeting pack, and confirmed commitments update the plan and action list. People negotiate priorities and authorise changes to their teams' commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Departments use different update habits, and the campaign plan lacks a consistently maintained source of status. Coordination problems also reflect competing incentives.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared task views, dependency fields, and reminders are standard configuration work. AI-assisted setup can reduce implementation effort, but the main requirement is a simpler shared update process.
tasks.still_hard: Dependencies can be informal, resource promises can be unreliable, and departments may optimise for different goals. Software cannot negotiate those conflicts.
tasks.human_edge: The manager builds trust, spots hidden resistance, and brokers workable compromises across teams.

ambition.what: A twice-weekly decision on the campaign's most consequential unresolved dependency.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less status chasing and duplicated reporting, leaving more time for early conflict resolution. Department leads retain resource authority; a delegated campaign escalation mandate would let the manager convene decisions sooner.

reach.task: Balance competing campaign priorities across the portfolio.
reach.learn: Capacity planning, opportunity cost, and criteria for stopping lower-value work.

reach.task: Maintain a dependency-led delivery plan.
reach.learn: Critical paths, contingency ownership, and readiness criteria.

evidence.claim: Shared project records, reminders, dependency views, and approval fields can handle routine coordination without a model loop.
Removing a duplicated status pack depends on stakeholders accepting the shared live view; it does not eliminate negotiation.

assumptions: Departmental leads enter short structured updates directly in the {PROJECT}.
Meetings use the live campaign status instead of a separate meeting pack.
No employee ranking or performance scoring is introduced.
Access estimates include team permissions and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which departments already maintain useful records in the {PROJECT}?
Will departmental leads accept shared status fields and update deadlines?
Who can change campaign milestones and commit departmental capacity?
Are external agencies allowed into the shared project view?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed visibility?
research_questions: Which recurring status questions can be answered directly from maintained records?
Which meetings resolve conflicts and which only repeat updates?
Which dependencies cause late surprises despite apparently green status?
new_work: Maintain owners, dependencies, and escalation thresholds.
Resolve stale or contradictory updates.
Review reminders that create noise.
Manage permissions and external collaboration boundaries.
tasks.statement: Coordinate activities of departments, such as sales, graphic arts, media, finance, and research.

tasks.short: Prepare advertising or sales contract drafts, negotiate terms, obtain approvals, and arrange signature.

steps.what: Collect the commercial brief, counterparty details, proposed terms, and approval limits.
Populate the approved contract template and attach the commercial schedule.
Review counterparty edits and identify commercial or legal departures from the draft.

loop.input: Document comparison, counterparty redline, approved clause library, and approval matrix.
loop.output: Draft deviation register with clause references and issues for negotiation or legal review.
loop.check: Reconcile against deterministic text differences; quote changed clauses and verify amounts and dates separately.
loop.stop: One classification and one repair per version; unknown clauses or unreadable text go to legal counsel.
loop.why_not_simpler: Text comparison finds edits but cannot reliably interpret varied clause wording or cross-clause consequences.

steps.what: Negotiate price, scope, rights, deadlines, cancellation terms, and remedies with the counterparty.
Review legal departures and approve or return the contract for revision.
Approve the commercial commitment against budget and delegated authority.
Check the final approved version and sign through the signature process.
File the signed contract and record obligations, payment milestones, and renewal dates.

tasks.design: A configured intake in {WORKFLOW} pulls counterparty details from {CRM} or {PROCUREMENT}, and a deterministic generator fills approved templates in {DOCS}. Document comparison plus a bounded loop prepares a sourced deviation register; people negotiate and approve legal and commercial terms. Version-bound approvals control the signature process in {ESIGN}, then populate contract records and obligation reminders in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Commercial details arrive incompletely, templates drift, and redlines require interpretation. Negotiations and approval authority cannot be reduced to document generation.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, template assembly, document comparison, and signature workflows already exist. AI-assisted coding reduces integration effort, while bounded clause classification helps reviewers focus their attention.
tasks.still_hard: Non-standard liability, intellectual-property rights, sales commitments, and cross-border terms need specialist judgement. Scanned documents and late changes complicate version control.
tasks.human_edge: The manager reads bargaining signals and trades concessions without damaging the commercial relationship; legal counsel judges acceptable legal exposure.

ambition.what: A pre-negotiation options brief showing approved concession packages and their commercial consequences.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time copying terms and comparing versions, and more time preparing concessions and negotiating. Signing and approval rights remain unchanged unless the organization explicitly delegates a wider commercial envelope.

reach.task: Assess the margin and delivery consequences of proposed promotional commitments.
reach.learn: Learn contribution economics, fulfillment constraints, and how concessions affect the campaign business case.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, deterministic contract assembly, version-bound approvals, and signature routing are feasible patterns.
Bounded redline classification can assist review, but the digest supplies no contract-specific product evidence or documented case.

assumptions: Advertising and sales contracts use separate templates and approval routes within the same contracting workflow.
For sales contracts, the budget owner represents the role authorized to approve commercial exposure.
The conversation-heavy prior is retained; contract paperwork and review preparation provide most of the time savings.
At least some approved templates and clause positions are available.
Only approved structured terms populate obligations automatically; bespoke obligations remain review items.
Build estimates cover two template families and existing signature access.
Access work includes GDPR requirements and consultation under national rules where employee-data use requires it.

Are approved clauses, concession limits, and escalation routes documented?
Which roles can negotiate, approve deviations, and sign?
Are contracts digitally readable, and where is the authoritative version stored?
Does a {CLM} already provide intake, assembly, comparison, and obligation tracking?
Which national contract and employee-consultation rules apply?

How well does deviation classification detect consequential edits in representative contract versions?
Can signature routing enforce approval against the exact final document version?
Which bespoke obligations require explicit human confirmation before scheduling?

Maintain approved templates, clause positions, and concession limits.
Resolve incomplete intake and unmatched counterparty records.
Test version binding after document or signature-system changes.
Review bespoke obligations and update reminders after amendments.
tasks.statement: Prepare and negotiate advertising and sales contracts.

tasks.short: Find suitable promotional contacts, make introductions, and develop relationships around shared campaign opportunities.

steps.what: Agree target buyers, partner profiles, and the proposed promotional offer.
Filter existing contacts and reconcile duplicate or incomplete records.
Research contact roles, audience fit, and relevant industry activity.

loop.input: A fixed set of permitted directory entries, partner materials, and contact records.
loop.output: Contact dossiers with source dates, roles, audience evidence, and missing facts.
loop.check: Require a source for each extracted fact; distinguish organisation facts from individual details; review uncertain identities.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per dossier; missing or conflicting facts enter an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Role descriptions and audience evidence appear in varied prose that fixed field mappings cannot reliably parse.

steps.what: Choose contacts and decide the introduction route.
Write and send a personal introduction or promotional invitation.

loop.input: Approved offer, verified contact dossier, introduction plan, and permitted relationship history.
loop.output: A short introduction draft using supported facts.
loop.check: Validate recipient eligibility and suppression status deterministically; manager approves recipient, wording, and any commitment before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per selected contact; uncertain eligibility blocks sending and returns to a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template cannot adequately express varied relationship context and a relevant personal introduction.

steps.what: Explore shared interests, build trust, and agree a possible collaboration.
Record relationship status, agreed actions, and follow-up dates.

tasks.design: Configure contact filtering, duplicate checks, structured meeting outcomes, and follow-up tasks in the {CRM}; a bounded extraction loop prepares source-linked dossiers from permitted material in the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares introductions, while the {WORKFLOW} checks contact permissions and suppression before a manager approves sending through the {EMAIL}. Relationship conversations stay with the manager, with agreed actions captured once.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relationship context was dispersed across personal mailboxes, contact records, and informal introductions. Contact filtering already existed, but source verification and personalised preparation took effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable contact records and follow-up rules can handle the structured work. Small extraction and drafting loops can process varied prose without delegating relationship ownership.
tasks.still_hard: Public information becomes stale, identities are ambiguous, and a relevant contact may have no interest or authority. Trust and permission to communicate cannot be inferred from a directory entry.
tasks.human_edge: Earn introductions, recognise mutual benefit, and sense when pursuing a contact would damage the relationship.

ambition.what: A quarterly promotional partnership programme for small regional distributors.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling dossiers and updating records, and more time on selected partner conversations. Authority to make commercial commitments remains within existing limits.

reach.task: Prepare a stakeholder relationship map for a promotional partnership.
reach.learn: Stakeholder interests, introduction etiquette, source verification, and relationship-sensitive communication.

HubSpot offers prospecting outreach generation; the proposed design retains approval before sending.
Electronic direct marketing is subject to consent requirements, applicable exceptions, and national implementation rules.
Direct-marketing objections must stop the relevant processing.

Approve personalised introductions and resolve eligibility exceptions.
Maintain duplicate rules, retention settings, and suppression synchronisation.
Keep structured relationship outcomes current after conversations.
tasks.statement: Identify and develop contacts for promotional campaigns and industry programs that meet identified buyer targets, such as dealers, distributors, or consumers.

tasks.short: Discuss advertising products, media choices, and contract constraints with department heads and staff.

steps.what: Gather campaign results, product priorities, contract constraints, and budget options into a briefing.
Arrange the discussion and circulate the briefing and questions.
Discuss trade-offs, clarify constraints, and work through disagreements with department heads and staff.
Write the decision summary, unresolved issues, and proposed actions.

loop.input: Discussion notes and proposed decision, without assuming meeting recording.
loop.output: Draft decision summary and actions with owners, dates, and unresolved issues.
loop.check: Trace each decision to notes; manager verifies attribution and separates proposals from approvals.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per meeting; unclear commitments remain explicitly unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Discussion notes express decisions and reservations in free text; templates alone cannot interpret them.

steps.what: Approve the selected product, media direction, or expenditure within delegated authority.
Assign approved actions and update the campaign plan.

tasks.design: A generator builds a sourced decision brief from {BI}, {ERP}, and approved records in {DOCS}, while {CALENDAR} and {WORKFLOW} arrange the discussion. A bounded loop drafts the decision summary from notes for manager review. Department-head approval activates the agreed actions in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation spans several sources, while the discussion depends on competing priorities and informal context. Meeting notes often blur proposals and final decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable brief templates and existing scheduling features remove routine preparation. A bounded drafting loop can organize notes without taking over the discussion.
tasks.still_hard: People may withhold concerns, change priorities, or disagree about authority. Source records cannot capture every political or commercial constraint.
tasks.human_edge: The manager draws out objections, builds agreement, and recognizes when apparent consensus is fragile.

ambition.what: A fortnightly decision session for stalled product-promotion choices.

tasks.altitude: More preparation arrives ready to inspect, leaving time for difficult conversations and follow-through. The manager can frame options more clearly; approval rights remain with the existing decision makers.

reach.task: Translate product priorities into an agreed campaign portfolio.
reach.learn: Learn contribution margins, positioning choices, and how competing campaigns affect shared budgets.

evidence.claim: Template-generated briefings, configured approvals, and reviewed note drafting are feasible; no task-specific case is supplied.
Campaign-plan drafting is commercially available, supporting preparation rather than delegated organizational decisions.

assumptions: The meeting remains the largest time share, consistent with the human-conversation prior.
Brief inputs are approved structured records or links; the generator exposes missing inputs rather than inventing them.
Discussion notes are available; recording and transcription are outside the initial scope.
Build ranges cover one briefing template and one approval route.
Consultation under national rules is assessed if meeting-data collection or staff monitoring expands.

Are campaign results and budgets available through governed exports or APIs?
How are decisions and action ownership recorded today?

Does note drafting preserve reservations and distinguish agreement from discussion in representative meetings?

Maintain briefing templates and source permissions.
Resolve missing owners, deadlines, and approval ambiguity.
Keep decision records aligned with subsequent changes.
tasks.statement: Confer with department heads or staff to discuss topics such as contracts, selection of advertising media, or product to be advertised.

tasks.short: Monitor promotion results and judge whether campaigns justify their costs.

steps.what: Export promotion responses and attributed sales.
Collect media spend, supplier charges, discounts, and campaign budget.
Match campaign identifiers and resolve missing costs or inconsistent reporting periods.
Calculate response rates, acquisition costs, contribution, and budget variance.
Judge cost effectiveness and recommend continuing, changing, or stopping the promotion.
Send the scorecard and recommendation to campaign stakeholders.

tasks.design: Configure feeds from {ADS}, {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, {CRM}, and {ERP}; use a mapping job on {DATA_PLATFORM} to reconcile campaign identifiers and reporting periods. A {BI} scorecard exposes source totals, missing costs, attribution assumptions, and approved metrics, while {WORKFLOW} routes exceptions and distributes the manager's recommendation. Spending changes remain separate approval actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Campaign identifiers, cost timing, and attribution definitions differ across systems. Existing reports often cover only one channel.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors and dashboard features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding makes the remaining mapping and reconciliation code cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Attributed sales do not establish incremental sales. Returns, delayed conversions, overlapping promotions, and incomplete margin data can change the conclusion.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether an apparent gain reflects real customer demand, discount subsidy, seasonality, or a weak comparison.

ambition.what: Daily pause-or-continue recommendations for active promotions with sufficiently fresh conversion and cost data.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling reports to investigating weak promotions and designing better comparisons. No spending authority changes automatically; faster recommendations go to the existing budget holder.

reach.task: Design a holdout test for promotion incrementality.
reach.learn: Comparison groups, sample size, uncertainty, and the difference between attribution and causation.

reach.task: Compare promotion contribution across the campaign portfolio.
reach.learn: Contribution margins, commercial constraints, and portfolio tradeoffs.

evidence.claim: Configured connectors and reporting tools can standardise channel data and automate marketing reports.
Marketing automation can report campaign responses and support questions about campaign data.
Identifier reconciliation and metric calculations can use deterministic rules; causal interpretation still requires judgement.

Time shares are illustrative task shares, not measured customer savings.
Structured inputs support substantial automation despite limited rule coverage for the final commercial judgement.
Build ranges cover an initial campaign family and existing connectors; shared foundations can support the other tasks.
GDPR applies to identifiable customer data. Aggregate reporting should be preferred where sufficient.

Are contribution margins, returns, and discount costs available at the required level?

Which campaigns support credible holdout or geographic comparisons?

Maintain metric definitions, cost allocations, and attribution windows.
Monitor connector failures and source schema changes.
Periodically compare attributed returns with experimental evidence.
tasks.statement: Monitor and analyze sales promotion results to determine cost effectiveness of promotion campaigns.

tasks.short: Read professional publications and identify developments that could change media plans.

steps.what: Find relevant articles through {EMAIL} subscriptions and a {OTHER} publication reader.
Read shortlisted articles and identify useful evidence.

loop.input: Licensed article text and media priorities.
loop.output: Claims, supporting passages, publication dates and relevance tags.
loop.check: Require exact supporting passages and valid source references; the manager reads consequential originals.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per article; unreadable or unsupported items return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword filters cannot reliably extract claims and qualifications from varied prose.

steps.what: Write a short evidence note in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Extracted passages, source references and manager annotations.
loop.output: A concise evidence note separating reported findings from possible implications.
loop.check: Every factual claim links to a passage; the manager approves the note before team circulation.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved claims are omitted or written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure but cannot condense varied findings into readable prose.

steps.what: Decide which developments merit a media test or planning change.

tasks.design: Configure subscriptions and deduplication in {WORKFLOW}, storing permitted source references in {DOCS}. Bounded extraction and drafting loops prepare a cited reading brief; the manager checks important originals and records test recommendations in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Subscriptions could collect material, but relevance assessment and useful notes still required reading across inconsistent publications.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing feed rules handle collection; bounded text extraction and cheaper custom integration reduce briefing effort.
tasks.still_hard: Paywalls, reuse rights, weak studies and claims that do not transfer to the company's audience.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising which apparent trend matters commercially, and which evidence is too weak to justify a test.

ambition.what: A weekly decision on whether one emerging media format deserves a small test.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less scanning and note writing, with more time for source checking and test design. Budget authority stays unchanged.
